title: Design Ride-Sharing Service (Uber)
subtitle: High-concurrency geospatial matching at global scale

stages.title: Stage 1 — Monolith & Relational DB
stages.bottleneck: Database reads/writes fail at scale. Querying active drivers using standard SQL `SELECT` with `WHERE distance < 5km` takes O(N) time — locking the DB at >100 concurrent requests.
stages.narrative:
**The simplest ride matching service.** Driver locations are updated every 4 seconds via HTTP POST and saved to PostgreSQL. When a rider requests a ride, the server does a bounding-box coordinate search using SQL index.

**Bottleneck:** High write volume (pings) from thousands of drivers locks rows. Geospatial queries scan the entire table, making it impossible to support more than a few hundred active users.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Geospatial Service & Redis Cache
stages.bottleneck: Drivers send pings every 4 seconds. Disk storage is overwhelmed. We need an in-memory Geospatial Index (Geohash) for driver locations.
stages.narrative:
**Introduce Spatial Indexing.** We move active driver locations from PostgreSQL to Redis. Redis has built-in geospatial data structures (`GEOADD` and `GEORADIUS`) based on **Geohash** (representing 2D coordinates as alphanumeric keys).

**Geohash logic:** Divide the world into grids. Adjacent points share prefixes. Lookups are O(log N) inside Redis memory, handling 100K+ reads/writes per second easily.

stages.title: Stage 3 — WebSockets & Dedicated Match Service
stages.bottleneck: Polled HTTP is slow and leads to wasted bandwidth. Match request timing out. We need real-time bi-directional messaging.
stages.narrative:
**Real-time matching.** Riders and drivers maintain persistent WebSocket connections. A dedicated Match Service matches requests asynchronously.

**The workflow:** Rider requests match → WS forwards to Match Service → Queries Geo Service for nearby drivers → Publishes ride offers to queue → WebSocket server pushes offer to driver immediately. If rejected, fallback to next driver.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Global Scale, Sharding by City
stages.bottleneck: At global scale, a single Redis cluster overflows. Kafka is needed for analytics/pings. Shard Geospatial index by city ID.
stages.narrative:
**Production scale.** Since riders and drivers are localized to cities (you can't match a rider in NY with a driver in SF), we **shard drivers by city ID**.

**Consistent Hashing:** Route WebSocket connections based on user location so adjacent cities share pools.

**Kafka integration:** Driver location updates are stream-written to Kafka, allowing multiple consumers (Matching, ETAs, Map data, and Fraud logs) to digest updates asynchronously without locking the critical path.
